task: Compare two factual household electricity-use regressors on the fixed real iFlex Phase 2 P-signal data. Use the same held-out outcomes and compare the incremental prediction value of the price features.
design_judgment: The comparison is suitable for observed residential electricity-use prediction under recorded price signals and available covariates. The current selected slice has four distinct offered amounts according to the parent data audit. The question is how well each model predicts the measured factual outcome and whether the price features improve that prediction.

iflex_primary_evidence.source: Hofmann and Siebenbrunner, Data in Brief 50, 109571 (2023), DOI 10.1016/j.dib.2023.109571
iflex_primary_evidence.finding: The source links recorded residential hourly smart-meter consumption, survey variables and regional temperature. The experiment tested hourly signals over two winter periods. Phase and signal filters define a particular subset of the original experimental support. The current four-amount count comes from the parent project audit of the selected P subset, not the full paper's set of price signals.

iflex_primary_evidence.source: Hofmann and Lindberg, Energy Policy 184, 113821 (2024), DOI 10.1016/j.enpol.2023.113821
iflex_primary_evidence.finding: The authors describe a reward scheme with one-day advance notice of hourly price signals. Their definition of a signal includes both peak price and the daily profile, including timing and duration. The full experiment's results concern response to those interventions. This comparison scores factual residential consumption on a restricted P subset.
iflex_primary_evidence.access: Publisher indexed abstract and authors' SSRN record were examined. The full publisher text and SSRN download page returned access errors in this review. The exact 2024 regression equations remain unverified.

iflex_primary_evidence.source: Hofmann and Lindberg, IEEE ISGT Europe (2021), DOI 10.1109/ISGTEurope52324.2021.9639976
iflex_primary_evidence.finding: The author-uploaded original full paper section III models group-hour electricity demand using group/time fixed effects and peak-price/nonpeak indicators, then replaces the peak indicator with separate indicators for specific signals. This is verified for the early experiment paper and is a treatment-response analysis, separate from the present factual prediction exercise.

The report distinguishes hourly signaled prices from the payout computed after consumption against a baseline. Use the announced signal as a predictive input and smart-meter kWh as the observed outcome. The post-outcome payout contains consumption information.

iflex_primary_evidence.source: Mohammadabadi, Skreiberg and Georges, Energy and Buildings 335, 115548 (2025)
iflex_primary_evidence.finding: Section 3.1 and equation 4 give a same-dataset example of load regression with ambient temperature and hour-specific models. Its analysis uses aggregate specific power and nonintervention observations, so its coefficients and errors do not transfer to the present P-signal, household-outcome comparison.

baseline.name: B1 polynomial-by-price spline Ridge outcome regression
baseline.verified_repo_structure: Degree-2 polynomial covariate features, training-fold StandardScaler, explicit evenly spaced cubic B-spline knots, and a design containing covariate terms, price-basis terms and their tensor interactions. Ridge fits measured Y. The original continuous configuration defaults to 6 spline knots and ridge alpha 0.1. These describe the existing source, not an assertion of the new frozen pilot settings.
baseline.role: Transfer the nuisance outcome learner structure and fit a factual conditional consumption regression on iFlex training rows. The continuous GPS, DR pseudo-outcome and second-stage smoother are separate components of the original Kennedy procedure.

candidate.name: scikit-learn 1.7.2 HistGradientBoostingRegressor with squared_error
candidate.role: Compare a histogram gradient-boosted tree conditional mean using the same raw prediction inputs. Each method can encode its features through its own fixed model structure. Squared error aligns candidate fitting with held-out RMSE for the common factual kWh target.
candidate.open_source: Pinned GitHub release tag 1.7.2, commit prefix 25dee60, September 2025 release confirmed by official 1.7 docs. Tagged COPYING explicitly says BSD 3-Clause. Official source and API are available. The pilot pins the parent-provided version for reproducibility.
candidate.early_stopping: Version 1.7.2 documents automatic stopping for more than 10000 training rows or explicit validation input. A fixed iteration setting with early_stopping=False, or a validation set consisting only of development blocks, keeps all decisions separate from final holdout. Internal per-row validation cannot stand in for independent date/household evaluation.

load_forecasting_precedent.source: Ben Taieb and Hyndman, International Journal of Forecasting 30(2), 382-394 (2014), DOI 10.1016/j.ijforecast.2013.07.005
load_forecasting_precedent.finding: The competition paper uses componentwise gradient boosting with penalized univariate spline learners for hourly zonal demand and weather/history/calendar inputs. It supports the practical pedigree of these model families. The scikit-learn lagged-feature example separately demonstrates HGB and temporal evaluation. Both are methodological precedents rather than performance estimates for this iFlex comparison.

support_boundary.continuous_DR: The selected offers are point masses. A continuous treatment density over unoffered amounts is incompatible with this empirical support. Local B1 config also defaults to min_unique_doses=20 and explicitly checks it in training folds. The full Kennedy estimator is outside this comparison.
support_boundary.spline_distinction: The old Ridge design uses B-splines as regression features with explicit knots, which differs from fitting SciPy make_smoothing_spline to pseudo-outcomes. SciPy requires at least five abscissas and the implementation checks that x is strictly increasing. Four unique amounts do not meet those conditions after duplicate aggregation. The Ridge feature map can still be fit and compared at recorded amounts.
support_boundary.reporting_extent: Report error for observed outcome predictions at recorded price configurations. Four price values provide no empirical validation for arbitrary intermediate amounts, a continuous price derivative or EV physical effective-response duration.

comparison_contract: Use the same frozen train/development/test design, outcome hours, kWh units, prediction features, missing-data cohort and scoring rows for both methods. Fit all learned preprocessing using training data. Keep all target-time variables to the information set stated in the prediction task. If weather is measured during the outcome window, describe predictions as conditional on observed weather rather than an operational day-ahead forecast.

Price ablation removes the declared prospective price columns and their model-specific transforms. If the features preserve signal labels or deterministic price encodings, name them and describe the result as the incremental value of the removed numeric price conditional on those remaining inputs. The ablation compares out-of-sample prediction error, which does not identify a causal effect.

Report paired absolute MAE/RMSE in kWh, output coverage, and the known held-out date/event/household structure. Repeated household rows at a common signal or date provide many factual outcomes but do not create independent experimental price assignments.

The result is residential consumption, including all metered household uses. A factual prediction gain can motivate studying the nuisance learner in a separate setting, but cannot substitute for an EV response-duration benchmark.
verification_scope: Only primary research, official software references and the existing continuous model source were inspected. This record contains no accessed final outcomes, fitted models or performance claims.
